resources.string: Current plays your own media from a Jellyfin server. Add its address to sign in.
Sign in to %1$s to see your libraries.
Signed in as %1$s on %2$s. Your libraries will appear here.
No servers yet. Add a Jellyfin server by its address.
You are signed out and the server is forgotten on this device. You can add it again later.
Sign-ins are kept in Windows Credential Manager.
Sign-ins are kept in your desktop's keyring, through the Secret Service.
Sign-ins are kept in this browser.
Sign-ins are kept in a file only your user account can read.
No credential store was found, so you are signed out when the app quits.
Copies the app version and the last requests to your servers, without addresses or passwords, to paste into a problem report.
%1$s is tried at these addresses from the top. The first one that answers is used.
%1$s does not answer at any of these addresses right now.
A server keeps at least one address, so this one cannot be removed.
Current stops trying this address. You can add it again later, while the server answers there.
Enter the address of your Jellyfin server, such as media.example.com or 192.168.1.10:8096.
This address is not encrypted (http on the internet). Your password and media would cross the internet readable by others. Use https if the server offers it.
That is not a server address.
No server answered. Check the address, the port and that the server is running.
The server took too long to answer.
The address redirects elsewhere. If the server runs under a path, include it (for example /jellyfin), or use https.
Something answered, but it is not a Jellyfin server.
Another server answers at this address.
This server is no longer saved.
Enter another address of %1$s, such as media.example.com or 192.168.1.10:8096. It is added only if %1$s answers there.
To reach a server on your home network, Current needs the permission Android calls "Nearby devices".
Without "Nearby devices", servers on your home network cannot be reached, even by an internet name that leads to them at home. Other servers on the internet still work.

"Nearby devices" is turned off for Current, so servers on your home network cannot be reached, even by an internet name that leads to them at home. Other servers on the internet still work. You can turn it on in the app's settings.
If this server is on your home network, or its name leads there at home, "Nearby devices" being off is the likely cause.
In another Jellyfin app where you are signed in, open Quick Connect and enter this code. This page continues by itself once you approve it.
The server took too long to answer.
Another server answers at this address now, so nothing was sent to it.
Quick Connect is turned off on this server.
This server is no longer saved.
